marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q019.takeaway: Primary bile acids are synthesized in hepatocytes from cholesterol.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q019.displayText:
Primary bile acids are synthesized in hepatocytes from cholesterol.

Primary bile acids are synthesized from cholesterol by hepatocytes.

Bile contains bile acids, bile salts, bile pigments, phospholipids, water, and electrolytes. It is secreted by the liver and concentrated in the gall bladder.

Two primary bile acids (cholic acid and chenodeoxycholic acid) are synthesized from cholesterol by hepatocytes. When these primary bile acids are secreted into the lumen of the intestine, a portion of each is converted to secondary bile acids (deoxycholic acid and lithocholic acid) by bacteria.

The liver conjugates primary and secondary bile acids with glycine or taurine to their respective bile salts. Examples: Glycocholic acid, Taurodeoxycholic acid.

Rate of bile secretion is 30-60 mL/hour (500-1000 mL/day).

Note: Bile has no digestive enzymes.
emphasis: Primary bile acids are synthesized in hepatocytes from cholesterol

rationales.b: Amino acids conjugate bile acids but are not the precursor from which primary acids are made.
rationales.c: Bilirubin is excreted in bile but does not form bile acids.
rationales.d: Fatty acids are not the substrate for primary bile-acid synthesis.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q020.takeaway: Enterohepatic recirculation conserves the bile-salt pool and is needed to sustain daily bile-salt secretion.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q020.displayText:
Enterohepatic recirculation conserves the bile-salt pool and is needed to sustain daily bile-salt secretion.

Enterohepatic circulation is necessary for the secretion of bile salts.

The enterohepatic circulation of bile salts is the recycling of bile salts between the small intestine (terminal ileum) and the liver by means of the portal vein. It occurs 6-8 times a day.

The recirculation of bile salts to the liver reduces the demand to synthesize new bile salts.
emphasis: Enterohepatic recirculation conserves the bile-salt pool and is needed to sustain daily bile-salt secretion

rationales.b: Intestinal juice is secreted by intestinal epithelium and does not depend on bile-salt recycling.
rationales.c: Pancreatic juice is controlled by secretin, CCK and vagal input.
rationales.d: Bilirubin is excreted in bile and is not recycled as a secreted bile-salt pool.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q021.takeaway: CCK belongs to the gastrin family; GIP, glucagon and VIP belong to the secretin-related peptide family.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q021.displayText:
CCK belongs to the gastrin family; GIP, glucagon and VIP belong to the secretin-related peptide family.

CCK (Cholecystokinin) belongs to the gastrin family, not the secretin family.

Classification of GI hormones based on structure and function:
• Gastrin family - Gastrin, Cholecystokinin
• Secretin family - Secretin, Glucagon, VIP, GIP
• Others - Motilin, Ghrelin, Somatostatin
emphasis: CCK belongs to the gastrin family; GIP, glucagon and VIP belong to the secretin-related peptide family

rationales.a: GIP is structurally grouped with secretin-family peptides.
rationales.b: Glucagon is related to secretin-family peptides.
rationales.d: VIP is a member of the secretin/glucagon peptide family.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q022.takeaway: Gastrin is a peptide hormone secreted primarily by antral G cells and trophically supports gastric mucosa.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q022.displayText:
Gastrin is a peptide hormone secreted primarily by antral G cells and trophically supports gastric mucosa.

Gastrin is a peptide hormone.

It is secreted by the G cells of the gastric mucosa present in the antrum of the stomach, primarily during the gastric phase of gastric acid secretion.

It causes gastric secretion at 1000-1500 mL/day. Its primary stimulus is gastric distension.

Primary functions of Gastrin:
• Gastric acid (HCl) secretion
• Pepsin secretion
• Trophic action on the gastric mucosa

Other functions:
• Stimulates gastric motility
• Prevents gastroesophageal reflux by contraction of LES

Conditions associated with increased gastrin secretions (Ex: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome), will cause an increase in H+ secretion and hypertrophy of the gastric mucosa.

Conditions associated with reduced gastrin secretion (Ex: Resection of the gastric antrum), will cause a decrease in H+ secretion and atrophy of the gastric mucosa.
emphasis: Gastrin is a peptide hormone secreted primarily by antral G cells and trophically supports gastric mucosa

rationales.a: Chief cells secrete pepsinogen, while antral G cells secrete gastrin.
rationales.c: Gastrin is stimulated by peptides and vagal GRP, not primarily released in cephalic phase.
rationales.d: Secretin inhibits gastrin/acid output rather than stimulating gastrin release.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q023.takeaway: CCK slows gastric emptying while contracting the gallbladder and stimulating pancreatic enzyme secretion.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q023.displayText:
CCK slows gastric emptying while contracting the gallbladder and stimulating pancreatic enzyme secretion.

Cholecystokinin (CCK) inhibits gastric emptying.

It is secreted by the I cells of the duodenal and jejunal mucosa in response to monoglycerides, fatty acids, and amino acids.

Primary functions:
• Stimulation of pancreatic enzyme secretion
• Contraction of the gallbladder
• Relaxation of the sphincter of Oddi

Other functions:
• Augmentation of the action of Secretin in producing alkaline (bicarbonate rich) pancreatic juice
• Inhibition of gastric emptying
• Trophic (growth) effect on the exocrine pancreas
• Increases the synthesis of enterokinase
• Enhances the motility of the small intestine and colon
• Along with secretin, augments contraction of the pyloric sphincter and thus prevents reflux of duodenal contents into the stomach
• Promotes satiety
emphasis: CCK slows gastric emptying while contracting the gallbladder and stimulating pancreatic enzyme secretion

rationales.a: CCK relaxes the sphincter of Oddi rather than contracting it.
rationales.d: CCK contracts, rather than relaxes, the gallbladder.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q024.takeaway: Acidic chyme in the duodenum stimulates S-cell release of secretin.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q024.displayText:
Acidic chyme in the duodenum stimulates S-cell release of secretin.

Secretin secretion is stimulated by acid.

Stimuli that increase secretin secretion:
• Low duodenal pH (2-4.5) due to acid in the chyme
• Products of protein digestion in the upper small intestine

Secretin secretion is regulated by negative feedback.
emphasis: Acidic chyme in the duodenum stimulates S-cell release of secretin

rationales.a: Epinephrine is not the primary luminal stimulus for secretin secretion.
rationales.c: Fat primarily stimulates CCK release from I cells.
rationales.d: Acetylcholine may modulate secretion but acid is the key direct stimulus.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q025.takeaway: The liver synthesizes albumin, clotting factors and acute-phase proteins, but immunoglobulins are made by plasma cells.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q025.displayText:
The liver synthesizes albumin, clotting factors and acute-phase proteins, but immunoglobulins are made by plasma cells.

Immunoglobulins are not synthesized by the liver. They are produced by plasma cells.

Plasma proteins synthesized by the liver are:
• Albumin
• Coagulation/clotting factors
• Acute-phase proteins
• Steroid binding and other hormone-binding proteins
emphasis: The liver synthesizes albumin, clotting factors and acute-phase proteins, but immunoglobulins are made by plasma cells

rationales.b: The liver synthesizes most coagulation factors.
rationales.c: The liver produces many acute-phase proteins.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q026.takeaway: Daily gastric juice secretion is approximately 1.5–2.0 L.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q026.displayText:
Daily gastric juice secretion is approximately 1.5–2.0 L.

Daily secretion of gastric juice is between 1500-2000 mL.

Note: This is a controversial question - Daily secretion of gastric juice is:
• 1500 mL according to Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th edition, Page no: 819
• 2500 mL according to Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 25th Edition, Page no: 464

Choose 2500 mL if given in the options. If not, choose within the range of 1500-2500 mL.
emphasis: Daily gastric juice secretion is approximately 1

rationales.a: 0.5–1.0 L is below the usual daily secretion.
rationales.c: 3–3.5 L is above the conventional daily volume.
rationales.d: 3.5–5 L substantially overestimates daily gastric secretion.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q027.takeaway: Secretin stimulates pancreatic duct cells to secrete bicarbonate-rich fluid.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q027.displayText:
Secretin stimulates pancreatic duct cells to secrete bicarbonate-rich fluid.

Secretin increases HCO3- secretion by ductal cells of the pancreas and duodenum. It is secreted by the S cells in the upper small intestine.

Functions of secretin are:
• Primary function
• ↑ HCO3- secretion by ductal cells of pancreas and duodenum
• Other functions
• Augments the effects of CCK
• Inhibits gastrin release
• ↓ gastric acid secretion
• Contraction of pyloric sphincter
• Exerts trophic effect on the pancreas
emphasis: Secretin stimulates pancreatic duct cells to secrete bicarbonate-rich fluid

rationales.b: Secretin increases rather than inhibits bicarbonate secretion.
rationales.c: Secretin suppresses gastric acid rather than increasing it.
rationales.d: Secretin does not stimulate gastrin; its main effect is pancreatic/ductal bicarbonate.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q028.takeaway: Duodenal I cells secrete CCK in response to fats and amino acids.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q028.displayText:
Duodenal I cells secrete CCK in response to fats and amino acids.

I cells of the duodenum secrete CCK.
emphasis: Duodenal I cells secrete CCK in response to fats and amino acids

rationales.a: Secretin is secreted by duodenal S cells.
rationales.b: Gastrin is produced by G cells, mainly in gastric antrum.
rationales.d: Motilin is secreted by M cells and helps regulate migrating motor complexes.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q029.takeaway: Gastrin is secreted mainly by G cells in the gastric antrum; gastrinoma causes severe acid-peptic disease.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q029.displayText:
Gastrin is secreted mainly by G cells in the gastric antrum; gastrinoma causes severe acid-peptic disease.

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. In this condition, serum gastrin concentration is raised to around >1000 pg/ml. Gastrin is primarily secreted by G cells present in the antrum of the stomach.
emphasis: Gastrin is secreted mainly by G cells in the gastric antrum; gastrinoma causes severe acid-peptic disease

rationales.a: The pyloric ring is an outlet structure; antral mucosa contains the principal G-cell population.
rationales.c: Pancreatic gastrinomas may occur, but normal gastrin secretion is primarily antral.
rationales.d: Small intestine has some endocrine cells but is not the principal gastrin source.

marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q030.takeaway: Gastrin is not a major pancreatic secretagogue; secretin and CCK strongly regulate pancreatic secretion.
marrow__PHYSIO_CH31_Q030.displayText:
Gastrin is not a major pancreatic secretagogue; secretin and CCK strongly regulate pancreatic secretion.

Gastrin does not act upon the pancreas. Gastrin stimulates gastric acid secretion and gastric mucosal growth.

GI hormones acting on the pancreas include CCK, Secretin and GIP.

GIP is also known as Glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide.
emphasis: Gastrin is not a major pancreatic secretagogue; secretin and CCK strongly regulate pancreatic secretion

rationales.a: Secretin stimulates ductal bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice.
rationales.d: GIP can modulate pancreatic endocrine secretion; gastrin is the keyed hormone not acting on pancreas in this comparison.
